claim: Fam49b-KO mice were generated by creating a premature stop codon in exon 6 of the Cyrib locus encoding Fam49b using CRISPR/Cas9.
source: To assess the role of Fam49b in T cell development, we generated Fam49b-KO mice by creating a premature stop codon in exon 6 of the Cyrib locus encoding Fam49b using CRISPR/Cas9 (Figure 1A).
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental method used to generate the knockout mice and references Figure 1A showing the genetic modification.

claim: Fam49a is a homologous protein that is ~80% identical to Fam49b.
source: Fam49a is a homologous protein that is ~80% identical to Fam49b that has also been suggested to be involved in lymphopoiesis in zebrafish (Li et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript states the sequence identity between Fam49a and Fam49b and cites a reference about Fam49a's role in zebrafish.

claim: Fam49a has been suggested to be involved in lymphopoiesis in zebrafish.
source: Fam49a is a homologous protein that is ~80% identical to Fam49b that has also been suggested to be involved in lymphopoiesis in zebrafish (Li et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Li et al., 2016.

claim: Fam49a-KO mice were generated by creating a stop codon in exon 7 of the Cyria locus encoding Fam49a.
source: We generated Fam49a-KO mice in a similar manner by creating a stop codon in exon 7 of the Cyria locus encoding Fam49a (Figure 1B).
evidence: The manuscript describes the method used to generate Fam49a-KO mice and references Figure 1B.

claim: Fam49a expression was undetectable in Fam49a-KO mice spleen tissues.
source: Immunoblot of spleen tissues confirmed that Fam49a or Fam49b expression was undetectable in Fam49a-KO mice or Fam49b-KO mice, respectively in contrast to the wild type (WT, C57BL/6 J) mice (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Fam49b expression was undetectable in Fam49b-KO mice spleen tissues.
source: Immunoblot of spleen tissues confirmed that Fam49a or Fam49b expression was undetectable in Fam49a-KO mice or Fam49b-KO mice, respectively in contrast to the wild type (WT, C57BL/6 J) mice (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Fam49b is expressed broadly throughout thymic development.
source: Real-time RT-PCR analysis of flow cytometry-sorted WT thymocytes subsets showed Fam49b is expressed broadly throughout thymic development, whereas Fam49a was mainly expressed in mature T cells (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data from sorted thymocyte subsets shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Fam49a was mainly expressed in mature T cells.
source: Real-time RT-PCR analysis of flow cytometry-sorted WT thymocytes subsets showed Fam49b is expressed broadly throughout thymic development, whereas Fam49a was mainly expressed in mature T cells (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Fam49a expression was not detectable in WT thymocytes.
source: The expression of Fam49a was not detectable in WT thymocytes (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Both Fam49a-KO and Fam49b-KO mice were fertile and did not show any apparent abnormalities.
source: Both Fam49a-KO and Fam49b-KO mice were fertile and did not show any apparent abnormalities.
evidence: The manuscript reports observational data about the general health and fertility of the knockout mice.

claim: The frequency and number of peripheral CD4+ T cells and CD8+ T cells were significantly reduced in Fam49b-KO mice compared to WT and Fam49a-KO mice.
source: Flow cytometry analysis of cells isolated from lymph nodes showed that the frequency and number of peripheral CD4+ T cells and CD8+ T cells were significantly reduced in Fam49b-KO mice (Figure 2A) compared to WT and Fam49a-KO mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The reduction in the number of CD8+ T cells was greater than that of CD4+ T cells in Fam49b-KO mice.
source: Notably, the reduction in the number of CD8+ T cells was greater than that of CD4+ T cells.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of data from Figure 2A.

claim: The ratio of CD4+ T cells over CD8+ T cells was increased in Fam49b-KO mice.
source: As a result, the ratio of CD4+ T cells over CD8+ T cells was increased in Fam49b-KO mice (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Fam49a-KO mice resembled WT mice in terms of T cell number and CD4/CD8 composition.
source: In contrast, Fam49a-KO mice resembled WT mice in terms of T cell number and CD4/CD8 composition.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of data from Figures 2A and 2B.

claim: The frequencies and numbers of CD4 SP and CD8 SP cells were reduced in Fam49b-KO mice thymi.
source: The frequencies and numbers of CD4 SP and CD8 SP cells were reduced and the ratios of CD4 SP to CD8 SP thymocytes were increased in Fam49b-KO mice thymi (Figure 2C and Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figures 2C and 2D.

claim: The ratios of CD4 SP to CD8 SP thymocytes were increased in Fam49b-KO mice thymi.
source: The frequencies and numbers of CD4 SP and CD8 SP cells were reduced and the ratios of CD4 SP to CD8 SP thymocytes were increased in Fam49b-KO mice thymi (Figure 2C and Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figures 2C and 2D.

claim: Fam49b deficiency leads to impaired thymocyte development for both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, with a more marked impact on the CD8+ T cell population.
source: These data indicate that Fam49b deficiency leads to impaired thymocyte development for both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, with a more marked impact on the CD8+ T cell population.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data presented in Figures 2C and 2D.

claim: Loss of Fam49a showed little, if any, impact on T cell numbers and cellularity in the periphery, or T cell thymic development.
source: In contrast, loss of Fam49a showed little, if any, impact on T cell numbers and cellularity in the periphery, or T cell thymic development.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of data from Figures 2A-2D.

claim: A lower frequency and the number of peripheral T cells was observed in Fam49b-KO chimera mice compared to WT chimera mice.
source: A lower frequency and the number of peripheral T cells (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–1B) and increased ratio of peripheral CD4+ T over CD8+ T was observed in Fam49b-KO chimera mice compared to WT chimera mice (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from bone marrow chimera experiments shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–1B.

claim: Increased ratio of peripheral CD4+ T over CD8+ T was observed in Fam49b-KO chimera mice compared to WT chimera mice.
source: A lower frequency and the number of peripheral T cells (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–1B) and increased ratio of peripheral CD4+ T over CD8+ T was observed in Fam49b-KO chimera mice compared to WT chimera mice (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The Fam49b-KO thymocytes developed in WT thymic environment are like those developed in the germline Fam49b-KO environment in terms of both thymocyte and peripheral lymphocyte phenotypes.
source: The Fam49b-KO thymocytes developed in WT thymic environment are like those developed in the germline Fam49b-KO environment in terms of both thymocyte and peripheral lymphocyte phenotypes (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of data from chimera and germline knockout mice shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–2C.

claim: The effect of Fam49b mutation on T cell development is predominantly due to thymocyte intrinsic functions.
source: Therefore, the effect of Fam49b mutation on T cell development is predominantly due to thymocyte intrinsic functions.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the bone marrow chimera data.

claim: The proportion of stage 1 thymocytes (TCRβloCD69-) were similar between WT and Fam49b-KO mice.
source: The proportion of stage 1 thymocytes (TCRβloCD69-), which include the DN and pre-selection DP cells, were similar between WT and Fam49b-KO mice.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of thymocyte subsets shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The percentage of stage 2 thymocytes (TCRβintCD69+) were significantly higher in the Fam49b-KO mice.
source: The percentage of stage 2 thymocytes (TCRβintCD69+), which represent transitional DP undergoing TCR-mediated positive selection, were significantly higher in the Fam49b-KO mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The proportion of late-stage thymocytes including the post-positive selection (TCRβhiCD69+) and the mature thymocytes (TCRβhiCD69-) were markedly decreased in Fam49b-KO mice.
source: The proportion of late-stage thymocytes including the post-positive selection (TCRβhiCD69+) and the mature thymocytes (TCRβhiCD69-) were markedly decreased (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Increased ratios of CD4 SP to CD8 SP were observed among the late-stage thymocytes (TCRβhiCD69+ and TCRβhiCD69-) in Fam49b-KO mice.
source: Consistent with our observation in the periphery, increased ratios of CD4 SP to CD8 SP were observed among the late-stage thymocytes (TCRβhiCD69+ and TCRβhiCD69-) in Fam49b-KO mice (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The post-positive-selection process is impaired in Fam49b-KO thymocytes.
source: These data show that the post-positive-selection process is impaired in Fam49b-KO thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data shown in Figures 3C and 3D.

claim: All the early phase populations (TCRβloCD5lo, TCRβloCD5int, TCRβintCD5hi) increased significantly in proportion in Fam49b-KO mice.
source: We observed that all the early phase populations (TCRβloCD5lo, TCRβloCD5int, TCRβintCD5hi) increased significantly in proportion in Fam49b-KO, whereas the post-positive selection SP thymocytes (TCRβhiCD5hi) were markedly decreased (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The post-positive selection SP thymocytes (TCRβhiCD5hi) were markedly decreased in Fam49b-KO mice.
source: We observed that all the early phase populations (TCRβloCD5lo, TCRβloCD5int, TCRβintCD5hi) increased significantly in proportion in Fam49b-KO, whereas the post-positive selection SP thymocytes (TCRβhiCD5hi) were markedly decreased (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: An increased ratio of CD4 SP to CD8 SP was observed in the post-positive selection population (TCRβhiCD5hi) in Fam49b-KO thymocytes.
source: Similarly, an increased ratio of CD4 SP to CD8 SP was observed in the post-positive selection population (TCRβhiCD5hi) in Fam49b-KO thymocytes (Figure 3F).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: A lower percentage of mature SP CD24loTCRβhi cells was observed in Fam49b-KO mice compared with WT mice.
source: This phenotype was further verified by the observation of lower percentage of mature SP CD24loTCRβhi cells in Fam49b-KO mice compared with WT mice (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Fam49b plays an important role in T cells development, especially in TCRβhiCD69+ and TCRβhiCD69- thymocytes.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that Fam49b plays an important role in T cells development, especially in TCRβhiCD69+ and TCRβhiCD69- thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data presented in Figures 3C-3G.

claim: The frequency of cells undergoing clonal deletion was increased among Fam49b-KO thymocytes.
source: We observed that the frequency of cells undergoing clonal deletion was increased among Fam49b-KO thymocytes, whereas the frequencies of cells to be eliminated through death by neglect were similar between Fam49b-KO and WT mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by cleaved caspase 3 staining data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The frequencies of cells to be eliminated through death by neglect were similar between Fam49b-KO and WT mice.
source: We observed that the frequency of cells undergoing clonal deletion was increased among Fam49b-KO thymocytes, whereas the frequencies of cells to be eliminated through death by neglect were similar between Fam49b-KO and WT mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by cleaved caspase 3 staining data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The frequencies of cleaved-caspase3+CCR7- cells and cleaved-caspase3+CCR7+ cells were significantly increased in the Fam49b-KO mice.
source: The frequencies of cleaved-caspase3+CCR7- cells and cleaved-caspase3+CCR7+ cells were significantly increased in the Fam49b-KO mice, suggesting that more thymocytes were eliminated through clonal deletion in both the cortex and medulla of Fam49b-KO thymus as compared with WT thymus (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: More thymocytes were eliminated through clonal deletion in both the cortex and medulla of Fam49b-KO thymus as compared with WT thymus.
source: The frequencies of cleaved-caspase3+CCR7- cells and cleaved-caspase3+CCR7+ cells were significantly increased in the Fam49b-KO mice, suggesting that more thymocytes were eliminated through clonal deletion in both the cortex and medulla of Fam49b-KO thymus as compared with WT thymus (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: CD5 expression was upregulated on Fam49b-KO DP thymocytes.
source: We found that CD5 expression was upregulated on Fam49b-KO DP thymocytes, but not on CD4 SP and CD8 SP thymocytes (Figure 4B), suggesting Fam49b-KO DP thymocytes had received stronger TCR signaling than the WT thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: CD5 expression was not upregulated on Fam49b-KO CD4 SP and CD8 SP thymocytes.
source: We found that CD5 expression was upregulated on Fam49b-KO DP thymocytes, but not on CD4 SP and CD8 SP thymocytes (Figure 4B), suggesting Fam49b-KO DP thymocytes had received stronger TCR signaling than the WT thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Fam49b-KO DP thymocytes had received stronger TCR signaling than the WT thymocytes.
source: We found that CD5 expression was upregulated on Fam49b-KO DP thymocytes, but not on CD4 SP and CD8 SP thymocytes (Figure 4B), suggesting Fam49b-KO DP thymocytes had received stronger TCR signaling than the WT thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation based on CD5 expression data shown in Figure 4B, using CD5 as a surrogate marker for TCR signal strength.

claim: Fam49b deficiency led to prolonged increases in all of the downstream phosphorylation events tested, including ZAP-70, LAT, PLCγ1, and ERK.
source: Fam49b deficiency led to prolonged increases in all of the downstream phosphorylation events tested, including ZAP-70, LAT, PLCγ1, and ERK (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: PAK phosphorylation was dramatically elevated in Fam49b-KO thymocytes.
source: PAK phosphorylation was also dramatically elevated in Fam49b-KO thymocytes (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Enhanced TCR-signaling strength intrinsic to Fam49b-KO DP thymocytes led to excessive clonal deletion in the cortex and medulla.
source: In summary, enhanced TCR-signaling strength intrinsic to Fam49b-KO DP thymocytes led to excessive clonal deletion in the cortex and medulla, resulting in the loss of naïve mature T cells in both thymus and periphery in the mice.
evidence: The claim is a summary interpretation of the data presented in Figures 4A-4D.

claim: Enhanced TCR-signaling strength intrinsic to Fam49b-KO DP thymocytes resulted in the loss of naïve mature T cells in both thymus and periphery in the mice.
source: In summary, enhanced TCR-signaling strength intrinsic to Fam49b-KO DP thymocytes led to excessive clonal deletion in the cortex and medulla, resulting in the loss of naïve mature T cells in both thymus and periphery in the mice.
evidence: The claim is a summary interpretation of the data presented in Figures 4A-4D.

claim: The absolute numbers of immature and mature CD8 SP and CD4 SP were decreased from Fam49b-KO mice.
source: Consistent with excessive clonal deletion in the cortex and medulla (Figure 4A), the absolute numbers of immature and mature CD8 SP and CD4 SP were decreased from Fam49b-KO mice (Figure 5A and Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figures 5A and 5B.

claim: IL-7Rα expression was significantly decreased in some Fam49b-KO CD4 SP thymocytes.
source: We observed that IL-7Rα expression was significantly decreased in some Fam49b-KO CD4 SP thymocytes, suggesting Fam49b deficiency could affect survival of SP thymocytes (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Fam49b deficiency could affect survival of SP thymocytes.
source: We observed that IL-7Rα expression was significantly decreased in some Fam49b-KO CD4 SP thymocytes, suggesting Fam49b deficiency could affect survival of SP thymocytes (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is an interpretation based on IL-7Rα expression data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: A twofold increase in cell death was observed in Fam49b-deficient immature and semi-mature SP thymocytes.
source: A twofold increase in cell death was observed in Fam49b-deficient immature and semi-mature SP thymocytes, whereas the frequency of dead cells detected among mature SP thymocytes was unaffected (Figure 5D and Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Annexin V/7-AAD staining data shown in Figures 5D, 5E, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–1B.

claim: The frequency of dead cells detected among mature SP thymocytes was unaffected in Fam49b-KO mice.
source: A twofold increase in cell death was observed in Fam49b-deficient immature and semi-mature SP thymocytes, whereas the frequency of dead cells detected among mature SP thymocytes was unaffected (Figure 5D and Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Annexin V/7-AAD staining data shown in Figures 5D, 5E, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–1B.

claim: Fam49b plays a key role in the maturation and maintenance of immature and semi-mature SP thymocytes.
source: Our results suggest that Fam49b plays a key role in the maturation and maintenance of immature and semi-mature SP thymocytes, but not in the survival of mature SP thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data presented in Figures 5A-5E.

claim: Fam49b does not play a key role in the survival of mature SP thymocytes.
source: Our results suggest that Fam49b plays a key role in the maturation and maintenance of immature and semi-mature SP thymocytes, but not in the survival of mature SP thymocytes.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data presented in Figures 5A-5E.

claim: There were no significant differences in frequencies and numbers of CD8 SP thymocytes in Fam49b-KO OT-I mice at 6 weeks.
source: However, contrary to the predictions, there were no significant differences in frequencies and numbers of CD8 SP thymocytes in Fam49b-KO OT-I mice at 6 weeks (Figure 6A and Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: Numbers of total CD8 T cells and naïve CD8 T cells were normal in 6 weeks old Fam49b-KO OT-I mice.
source: Numbers of total CD8 T cells and naïve CD8 T cells were, again, normal in 6 weeks old Fam49b-KO OT-I mice.
evidence: The claim is based on data shown in Figures 6C and 6D.

claim: The numbers of total CD8 T cells and naïve CD8 T cells were significantly decreased in Fam49b-KO OT-I mice at 12 weeks.
source: Interestingly, however, the numbers of total CD8 T cells and naïve CD8 T cells were significantly decreased in Fam49b-KO OT-I mice at 12 weeks. (Figure 6C and Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figures 6C, 6D, and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The frequency of Annexin V+ 7-AAD+ naïve CD8 T cells were significantly increased in spleen and lymph nodes from Fam49b-KO OT-I mice as well as Fam49b-KO mice.
source: We found that the frequency of Annexin V+ 7-AAD+ naïve CD8 T cells weresignificantly increased in spleen and lymph nodes from Fam49b-KO OT-I mice as well as Fam49b-KO mice (Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), suggesting Fam49b deficiency promotes naïve CD8 T cells death in the peripheral.
evidence: The claim is supported by Annexin V/7-AAD staining data shown in Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Fam49b deficiency promotes naïve CD8 T cells death in the peripheral.
source: We found that the frequency of Annexin V+ 7-AAD+ naïve CD8 T cells weresignificantly increased in spleen and lymph nodes from Fam49b-KO OT-I mice as well as Fam49b-KO mice (Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), suggesting Fam49b deficiency promotes naïve CD8 T cells death in the peripheral.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: A higher ratio of BIM/Bcl-2 is detected in naïve T cells as well as total thymocytes from Fam49b-KO mice.
source: We observed that a higher ratio of BIM/Bcl-2 is detected in naïve T cells as well as total thymocytes (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–B.

claim: Fam49b is required for peripheral T cells survival and maintenance.
source: In summary, these data show that Fam49b is required for peripheral T cells survival and maintenance.
evidence: The claim is a summary interpretation of the data presented in Figures 6A-6E and supplementary figures.

claim: The percentage of CD8αα+TCRαβ+ IELs among IEL T cells was significantly decreased from 60% in WT mice to 30% in Fam49b-KO mice.
source: The percentage of CD8αα+TCRαβ+ IELs among IEL T cells was significantly decreased from 60% in WT mice to 30% in Fam49b-KO mice, whereas the frequency of liver iNKT cells was unaffected (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The frequency of liver iNKT cells was unaffected in Fam49b-KO mice.
source: The percentage of CD8αα+TCRαβ+ IELs among IEL T cells was significantly decreased from 60% in WT mice to 30% in Fam49b-KO mice, whereas the frequency of liver iNKT cells was unaffected (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The frequency of Treg among lymph node CD4+ T cells increased slightly from 16 to 20% in lymph nodes in Fam49b-KO mice.
source: The frequency of Treg among lymph node CD4+ T cells increased slightly from 16 to 20% in lymph nodes in Fam49b-KO mice, though the absolute number of Treg was ~80% of the number in WT mice.
evidence: The claim is based on data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The absolute number of Treg was ~80% of the number in WT mice in Fam49b-KO mice.
source: The frequency of Treg among lymph node CD4+ T cells increased slightly from 16 to 20% in lymph nodes in Fam49b-KO mice, though the absolute number of Treg was ~80% of the number in WT mice.
evidence: The claim is based on data shown in Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Enhanced frequency of Treg in Fam49b-KO mice seems to be a result of a greater reduction of total CD4+ T cells compared to Treg.
source: Enhanced frequency of Treg seems to be a result of a greater reduction of total CD4+ T cells compared to Treg (Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Fam49b-KO mice showed a substantial reduction of natural IELs, including both the TCRγδ+ IELs as well as CD8αα+TCRαβ+ IELs.
source: Fam49b-KO mice showed a substantial reduction of natural IELs, including both the TCRγδ+ IELs as well as CD8αα+TCRαβ+ IELs (Figure 7B), whereas the relative frequencies of induced IELs (CD8αβ+TCRαβ+ IELs) were increased (Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The relative frequencies of induced IELs (CD8αβ+TCRαβ+ IELs) were increased in Fam49b-KO mice.
source: Fam49b-KO mice showed a substantial reduction of natural IELs, including both the TCRγδ+ IELs as well as CD8αα+TCRαβ+ IELs (Figure 7B), whereas the relative frequencies of induced IELs (CD8αβ+TCRαβ+ IELs) were increased (Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7C and Figure 7—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Fam49b is involved in shaping the agonist-selected unconventional T cell populations.
source: These results suggest that Fam49b is involved in shaping the agonist-selected unconventional T cell populations and that Fam49b deficiency leads to substantial loss of the natural IELs, including CD8αα+TCRαβ+ IELs and TCRγδ+ IELs.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data presented in Figures 7A-7C.

claim: Fam49b deficiency leads to substantial loss of the natural IELs, including CD8αα+TCRαβ+ IELs and TCRγδ+ IELs.
source: These results suggest that Fam49b is involved in shaping the agonist-selected unconventional T cell populations and that Fam49b deficiency leads to substantial loss of the natural IELs, including CD8αα+TCRαβ+ IELs and TCRγδ+ IELs.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the data presented in Figures 7A-7C.

claim: There was no decrease in the frequencies and numbers of two CD8αα IELps in the thymus of Fam49b-KO mice.
source: Contrary to our expectations, there was no decrease in the frequencies and numbers of two CD8αα IELps in the thymus (Figure 7—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The integrin expression of each CD8αα IELps was comparable between WT and Fam49b-KO mice.
source: The integrin expression of each CD8αα IELps was also comparable between WT and Fam49b-KO mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 3B–3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3B–3C.

claim: The lower number of CD8αα+TCRαβ+ IELs may be the result of impaired maintenance or survival in the periphery, rather than a problem with thymic IELps development.
source: We found that Fam49b is also required for the maintenance and survival of peripheral T cells (Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1). Therefore, we reasoned that the lower number of CD8αα+TCRαβ+ IELs may be the result of impaired maintenance or survival in the periphery, rather than a problem with thymic IELps development.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation based on the data from Figures 6, 7, and supplementary figures.

claim: Fam49b has been identified as an inhibitor of TCR signaling through binding with active Rac-1/2 in Fam49b-KO Jurkat T cells.
source: Fam49b has been identified as an inhibitor of TCR signaling through binding with active Rac-1/2 in Fam49b-KO Jurkat T cells (Shang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Shang et al., 2018.

claim: Lack of Fam49b led to hyperactivation of Jurkat T cells following TCR stimulation, as measured by the enhancement of CD69 induction, Rac-PAK axis signaling, and cytoskeleton reorganization.
source: Those studies showed that lack of Fam49b led to hyperactivation of Jurkat T cells following TCR stimulation, as measured by the enhancement of CD69 induction, Rac-PAK axis signaling, and cytoskeleton reorganization (Shang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Shang et al., 2018.

claim: Fam49b-KO double positive (DP) thymocytes underwent excessive negative selection.
source: We observed that Fam49b-KO double positive (DP) thymocytes underwent excessive negative selection, whereas the positive selection stage was unaffected.
evidence: The claim is based on data presented in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: The positive selection stage was unaffected in Fam49b-KO mice.
source: We observed that Fam49b-KO double positive (DP) thymocytes underwent excessive negative selection, whereas the positive selection stage was unaffected.
evidence: The claim is based on data presented in Figure 3.

claim: Fam49b deficiency impaired the survival of single positive thymocytes and peripheral T cells.
source: Fam49b deficiency impaired the survival of single positive thymocytes and peripheral T cells.
evidence: The claim is based on data presented in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: This altered development process resulted in significant reductions in CD4 and CD8 single-positive thymocytes as well as peripheral T cells.
source: This altered development process resulted in significant reductions in CD4 and CD8 single-positive thymocytes as well as peripheral T cells.
evidence: The claim is based on data presented in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: A large proportion of the TCRγδ+ and CD8αα+TCRαβ+ gut intraepithelial T lymphocytes were absent in Fam49b-KO mice.
source: Interestingly, a large proportion of the TCRγδ+ and CD8αα+TCRαβ+ gut intraepithelial T lymphocytes were absent in Fam49b-KO mice.
evidence: The claim is based on data presented in Figure 7.

claim: Fam49b dampens thymocytes TCR signaling in order to escape negative selection during development.
source: Our results demonstrate that Fam49b dampens thymocytes TCR signaling in order to escape negative selection during development, uncovering the function of Fam49b as a critical regulator of the selection process to ensure normal thymocyte development and peripheral T cells survival.
evidence: The claim is a summary interpretation of all the data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Fam49b is a critical regulator of the selection process to ensure normal thymocyte development and peripheral T cells survival.
